key_insight: PI-GMDH adaptively builds the functional form of the solution while enforcing physics, rather than optimizing only fixed architectures.
engineering_relevance: This can reduce model size and training cost for CFD surrogates or inverse problems while maintaining strong accuracy on benchmark incompressible flows.
method: Progressively constructs coupled field representations by adding candidate basis functions during training.
Ranks candidate directions using the first variation of a combined physics and observational objective.
Refines coefficients with block-coordinate damped Gauss-Newton optimization.
evidence_signal: On the 2D time-dependent Taylor-Green Navier-Stokes benchmark, adaptive PI-GMDH achieved validation and test losses of 5.299e-19 and 5.296e-19 with 204, 201, and 175 active functions for u, v, and p.
watch_item: The reported gains come from a controlled synthetic benchmark, so the results may not generalize directly to noisier or more complex real-world flow data.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Method of Group Data Handling: Adaptive Construction of Functional Representations with an Application to the Navier-Stokes Equations
